findings: MINOR: orchestrator run() checks only the first and last run_code_cell outputs and never asserts len(runs) == len(cells); a worker that legitimately stops after the CPU cell (e.g., reporting Drive absent, as the prompt instructs) yields status COMPLETE with the CPU-check JSON as 'remote'. Recovery is safe (poll shows STARTING; start always uses a fresh exclusive job) and there is no privacy/authority impact, but an execution-count assertion is recommended.

MINOR: reconcile() uses os.walk without onerror, so unreadable subdirectories are silently skipped while scan_complete remains True, overstating scan coverage; candidates() handles this correctly with onerror. Affects metadata accuracy only.

INFORMATIONAL: an identity.json binding mismatch (expected_binding_matches False, missing, or unparseable) is durably recorded in the receipt but does not block copying; the reviewed in-source SIZE/MD5 pin remains the operative verification authority, so this is a defensible design choice worth confirming as intended.

INFORMATIONAL: run() catches BaseException (including SystemExit/KeyboardInterrupt) without re-raising, so the process exits 0 on failure; the BLOCKED_OR_FAILED receipt status, not the exit code, is the source of truth, consistent with poll semantics. Failed copies also intentionally retain partial multi-GB files with no cleanup authority, which can consume Drive quota across repeated failures despite the SIZE+1GiB headroom check.

VERIFIED: fail-closed boundaries throughout — exclusive 'xb' destination and mkdir(0o700) job creation prevent overwrite and start-retry; incomplete Drive search raises instead of copying; destination checksum failure raises and preserves both original and partial; CPU/Colab and Drive-mount gates block before any work; inspect() enforces TOCTOU stability (inode/size/mtime before and after read) and symlinks are refused in all walkers and file reads.

VERIFIED: privacy of persistent artifacts — umask 0o077, 0o600 orchestrator logs, exception text and tracebacks confined to private console/stderr logs with only the exception class name in receipt.json/status.json; receipt content is limited to fixed paths, sizes, checksums, timestamps, and sanitized enums (whitelisted recorded_status, type-checked PID), so no arbitrary file content or patient data can leak into it.

VERIFIED: approval preservation and identity bindings — reviewed() pins verdict, scope, reviewed commit, reviewer model claude-fable-5, the response file's own sha256, and per-file sha256 of all three sources, so any source change invalidates the approval; the poll cell re-binds the deployed verify.py hash to the currently reviewed source; the job-path fullmatch regex plus repr() prevents cell-source injection; the worker is confined to colab-worker MCP tools with transcript-verified cell sources and no dispatch capability.

NOTE: source-only review; tests were read but not executed. verify_cell_sources, tool_exchanges, streams, private_dir, and write_private are imported from modules outside the supplied scope and were assumed to behave as their call sites imply.
